questions.prompt: Why is **data leakage** a critical bug when preprocessing before `train_test_split`?

options.text: Fitting scalers or imputers on the full dataset leaks test-set statistics into training, inflating validation scores

questions.prompt: What does `df.fillna(df['age'].median())` do?

options.text: Replaces missing `age` values with the column's median

questions.prompt: Why does **stratified** splitting (`stratify=y`) matter for imbalanced classification?

options.text: It preserves the same class proportions in both training and test splits

Assuming the null hypothesis is true, observing a difference at least this extreme has probability < 5%

options.text: Repeatedly testing without sequential correction inflates the false-positive rate well above 5%

Dropping a column that is 98% empty and uninformative

Adding a binary `was_missing` indicator alongside imputation when missingness itself carries signal

questions.prompt: What is the **learning rate** (`lr`) in gradient descent?

options.text: The step size scaling each parameter update along the negative gradient

questions.prompt: Why do **Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)** work well on images compared to plain dense MLPs?

options.text: Shared local filters exploit spatial locality and translation equivariance with far fewer parameters

options.text: Sparse models where irrelevant feature weights shrink to exact zero

questions.prompt: In **k-Means clustering**, why must numeric features be scaled beforehand?

options.text: Euclidean distance is dominated by whichever feature has the largest numeric scale

Computing rolling/lag features strictly from past timestamps

questions.prompt: What is **hyperparameter tuning** (e.g., Grid Search or Randomized Search)?

options.text: Searching model configuration settings (like `max_depth` or `C`) using validation performance

questions.prompt: Why is **precision-recall AUC (PR-AUC)** often preferred over **ROC-AUC** for rare-event detection?

options.text: ROC-AUC's false-positive rate denominator includes huge true negatives, masking poor precision on rare positives

questions.prompt: What is **early stopping**?

options.text: Halting iterative training when validation loss stops improving for `patience` epochs

columns.label: Grid/spatial data such as images and spectrograms
Sequence and language modeling via self-attention

questions.prompt: What does **SMOTE** or **class weighting** (`class_weight='balanced'`) address?

options.text: Severe class imbalance where the minority class is under-weighted by standard loss functions

questions.prompt: Why should you fix a **`random_state` / seed** in experiments?

options.text: To make splits, initializations, and shuffled results reproducible across runs

questions.prompt: What is **multicollinearity** in linear regression?

options.text: High correlation among predictor features, making individual coefficient estimates unstable

questions.prompt: What does **dimensionality reduction (PCA)** do?

options.text: Projects correlated features onto orthogonal principal components capturing maximum variance

questions.prompt: Which checks should run before trusting a **high validation score**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Verify no target-leaking feature (recorded after the prediction event) slipped in
Check for duplicate/near-duplicate rows spanning train and test splits
Verify preprocessing was fit inside cross-validation folds

questions.prompt: In **gradient descent**, what is the **vanishing gradient** problem?

options.text: Gradients shrink exponentially toward zero through deep layers, stalling early-layer learning

questions.prompt: What is **transfer learning**?

options.text: Training from scratch with random weights every time
Reusing a model pre-trained on a large dataset and fine-tuning it on a smaller target task

questions.prompt: What is **Simpson's paradox** in data analysis?

options.text: A trend that appears in aggregated data but reverses when the data is stratified by a confounding subgroup

questions.prompt: What does `cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=5)` return in scikit-learn?

options.text: An array of 5 validation scores, one per held-out fold

code.source: scores = cross_val_score(clf, X, y, cv=5, scoring='f1')

questions.prompt: Why is **calibration** (e.g., Brier score / reliability curve) important when a model outputs probabilities?

options.text: To ensure predicted `0.80` actually corresponds to ~80% positive outcomes when decisions depend on expected value

questions.prompt: What is **k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN)**'s main scaling weakness at inference time?

options.text: Prediction must search distances against stored training points, slowing down as N and dimensions grow

questions.prompt: Which fairness/privacy concerns require review in **responsible AI**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Memorization/leakage of sensitive training records by large models
Using zip code or proxy variables that encode protected attributes
Disparate error rates across protected demographic groups

questions.prompt: What is **differential privacy**?

options.text: Adding calibrated statistical noise so queries/models reveal aggregate patterns without exposing whether any single individual is in the dataset

questions.prompt: In `scikit-learn`, what is the difference between `.fit_transform(X_train)` and `.transform(X_test)`?

options.text: `.fit_transform` learns statistics from training data and applies them; `.transform` applies those learned statistics to test data without refitting

questions.prompt: What is **residual connection** (skip connection) in deep networks?

options.text: Adding a layer's input directly to its output (`F(x) + x`) to ease gradient flow in very deep networks

questions.prompt: When should you prefer a **simple baseline** (e.g., Logistic Regression or heuristic) before deep learning?

options.text: Never — always start with the largest transformer
Always — a fast interpretable baseline validates the pipeline, sets a benchmark, and may already meet requirements

questions.prompt: What is **model drift** (concept/data drift) in production ML?

options.text: Degradation in model accuracy over time as real-world input distributions or user behavior shift away from training data
